{{Short description|None}}
{{Use Canadian English|date=January 2023}}
[[File:Flag of Newfoundland and Labrador.svg|thumb|right|250px|Flag of Newfoundland and Labrador]]
The [[premier of Newfoundland and Labrador]] is the current title of the [[first minister]] for the [[Provinces and territories of Canada|Canadian province]] of [[Newfoundland and Labrador]], which was at certain points in its was history a [[Newfoundland Colony|colony]] and [[Dominion of Newfoundland|dominion]]. Newfoundland had a system of [[responsible government]] from 1855 to 1934, and again since 1949. Originally becoming a British [[crown colony]] in 1855, it would transition to a Dominion in 1907, and since 1949, a province of Canada. Since then, the province has been a part of the Canadian federation and has kept its own legislature to deal with provincial matters. The province was named Newfoundland and Labrador on December 6, 2001.<ref name="history">{{cite web|access-date=21 May 2013 |url=http://www.collectionscanada.gc.ca/confederation/023001-2230-e.html |date=2 May 2005 |title=Newfoundland |publisher=Library and Archives Canada |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080608210845/http://www.collectionscanada.gc.ca/confederation/023001-2230-e.html |archive-date=8 June 2008 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Newfoundland's name change now official |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/newfoundland-s-name-change-now-official-1.279040 |date=December 6, 2001 |access-date=2025-06-01 |website=[[CBC News]]}}</ref>

The province has a unicameral [[Westminster-style]] [[parliamentary government]], in which the premier is the leader of the party that controls the most seats in the [[Newfoundland and Labrador House of Assembly|House of Assembly]]. The premier is Newfoundland and Labrador's [[head of government]], and the [[king of Canada]] is its [[head of state]] and is represented by the [[lieutenant governor of Newfoundland and Labrador]]. The premier picks a cabinet from the elected members to form the [[Executive Council of Newfoundland and Labrador]], and presides over that body. Members are first elected to the House during [[List of Newfoundland and Labrador general elections|general elections]]. General elections must be conducted every four years from the date of the last election. An election may also take place if the governing party loses the confidence of the legislature by the defeat of a supply bill or tabling of a confidence motion.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=November 12, 2008|url=https://www.assembly.nl.ca/pubinfo/history.htm|title=History of the House of Assembly |publisher=Newfoundland and Labrador House of Assembly }}</ref>

From 1855 to 1907, the position of first minister was known as [[premier]]. After the colony was granted dominion status, the position became known as prime minister.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=November 12, 2008|url=https://www.heritage.nf.ca/govhouse/governorship/colonial.html|title=Colonial Governors, 1855-1933  |publisher=Memorial University of Newfoundland }}</ref> Democratic government was suspended in 1934 and replaced by an appointed [[Commission of Government]], until 1949 Newfoundland became a province of Canada. Since the reinstitution of democratic government in 1949, the title of first minister has been premier.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=November 12, 2008|url=https://www.heritage.nf.ca/govhouse/governorship/lieutenant.html|title=Lieutenant-Governors, 1949-Present  |publisher=Memorial University of Newfoundland }}</ref>

Since 1855, Newfoundland and Labrador has been led by ten Colonial premiers, nine Dominion prime ministers, three chairmen of Commission of Government, and sixteen provincial premiers. Of the provincial premiers, eight are from the [[Liberal Party of Newfoundland and Labrador|Liberal Party]], and eight are from the [[Progressive Conservative Party of Newfoundland and Labrador|Progressive Conservative Party]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Prime Ministers and Premiers of Newfoundland & Labrador |url=https://assembly.nl.ca/pdfs/PrimeMinistersPremiersNL.pdf |access-date=2025-06-01 |website=House of Assembly - Newfoundland and Labrador}}</ref>

==Dominion Prime Ministers of Newfoundland (1907–1934)==
By [[Royal Proclamation]], the colony was granted [[dominion]] status on 26 September 1907 becoming the [[Dominion of Newfoundland]] with its head of government being given the title Prime Minister of the Dominion of Newfoundland.

==Chairmen of the Commission of Government (1934–1949)==
With the suspension of [[responsible government]] the [[dominion]] was administered by the [[Commission of Government]], from 1934 to 1949. It was a body of seven appointed by the British government, made up of three British officials, three Newfoundlanders, and chaired by the Governor of Newfoundland.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=12 November 2008|url=https://www.heritage.nf.ca/govhouse/governorship/commission.html|title=Commission Governors, 1934-1948 |publisher=Memorial University of Newfoundland }}</ref>
